issues.title: [WO-001] Create the devcontainer and reproducible development toolchain
issues.body:
<!-- wallet-observer-task:WO-001 -->

**Milestone:** First live

**Plan:** [BUILD_PLAN.md](https://github.com/nhattruong0204/wallet-observer/blob/main/BUILD_PLAN.md)

**Website first (2026-10-05):** Deliver the desktop-browser website and its supporting services. Native mobile apps, installable PWA features, device push, mobile-specific UX and mobile acceptance gates are deferred. Existing responsive behavior may remain. See the [scope decision](https://github.com/nhattruong0204/wallet-observer/blob/main/docs/decisions/0003-website-first.md).

## Why we need this

A consistent environment lets you and Astra reproduce the same install, database connection, lint results, and debugging behavior across Windows/WSL and Linux.

## What to do

- Create a devcontainer with Python, Node, Git, PostgreSQL client tools, and a non-root development user.
- Define a development Compose setup and documented task commands; keep production configuration separate.

## How to implement

1. Use a supported Python release and Node LTS; pin the chosen versions and lock dependency resolutions. Record selections in docs/development.md.
2. Configure .devcontainer/devcontainer.json, a development Dockerfile, and a PostgreSQL service with a named volume and healthcheck. Forward only development ports.
3. Install dependencies through uv and the selected JavaScript package manager. Add Python/TypeScript formatting, linting, and editor debug configurations.
4. Provide placeholder environment variables and an explicit setup command. Do not put API keys or personal watchlists in images, tracked files, or lifecycle-hook output.

## Expected files and deliverables

- `.devcontainer/devcontainer.json`
- `.devcontainer/Dockerfile`
- `compose.dev.yml`
- `.env.example`
- `docs/development.md`

## Dependencies

None. Start here.

## Definition of done

- [x] A clean clone opens in the devcontainer and the non-root user can edit files.
- [x] Python, Node, package managers, and PostgreSQL client versions are documented and reproducible.
- [x] The database healthcheck succeeds and survives a container restart.
- [x] Setup commands succeed without paid credentials; provider-dependent commands report what is missing.
- [x] Documented Windows/WSL and Linux startup instructions contain no unimplemented success claims.

## Completion evidence

Attach or link the implementation PR, relevant commands/results or fixture checks, updated documentation, and remaining limitations. Distinguish real-provider verification from fixture-only checks.

## Verified WO-001 result

Development environment completed on 3 October 2026. See the [acceptance record](https://github.com/nhattruong0204/wallet-observer/blob/main/docs/acceptance/WO-001.md) and [development guide](https://github.com/nhattruong0204/wallet-observer/blob/main/docs/development.md).

A clean clone passed the Dev Containers CLI lifecycle, non-root workspace access, pinned version checks, locked bootstrap, database connectivity/persistence, lint/format checks, and all 7 tooling tests. Repeated bootstrap preserved both lockfiles and the existing local configuration. Windows desktop and ARM64 execution were not manually tested. Application implementation and real-provider qualification remain subsequent issues.

issues.title: [WO-002] Qualify the Solana data source and capture representative fixtures
issues.body:
<!-- wallet-observer-task:WO-002 -->

**Milestone:** First live

**Plan:** [BUILD_PLAN.md](https://github.com/nhattruong0204/wallet-observer/blob/main/BUILD_PLAN.md)

**Website first (2026-10-05):** Deliver the desktop-browser website and its supporting services. See the [scope decision](https://github.com/nhattruong0204/wallet-observer/blob/main/docs/decisions/0003-website-first.md).

## Why we need this

First-live estimates depend on a feed that actually covers the watched wallets, supported swap routes, and reconnect recovery. Writing the UI before proving this can leave a convincing but unusable application.

## What to do

- Evaluate one primary Solana provider and its decoded stream plus historical lookup capabilities.
- Define the supported execution types, coverage limits, rate/credit budget, and recovery strategy before implementing the collector.

## How to implement

1. Start with Helius Parsed Streams and its current official documentation; verify account filtering, supported programs, credentials, and confirmation fields against real payloads. Treat decoded instructions as inputs, not automatic proof of a buy.
2. Use a small user-supplied wallet list. Capture sanitized examples of a buy, sell, ordinary transfer, failed transaction, multi-leg swap, wrapped SOL flow, duplicate delivery, and unsupported route.
3. Prove how to recover events after disconnects. If the stream lacks replay, qualify a history endpoint and a bounded overlap/backfill strategy.
4. Measure delivery delay and credit usage for an explicitly recorded sample interval. Document unavailable FOMO-specific fields separately; do not use Wind endpoints as the backend.

## Expected files and deliverables

- `docs/data-source-contract.md`
- `docs/decisions/0001-solana-source.md`
- `tests/fixtures/solana/`

## Dependencies

- [WO-001](https://github.com/nhattruong0204/wallet-observer/issues/1)

## Definition of done

- [x] docs/data-source-contract.md names the chosen feed, credential mechanism, supported programs, commitment, rate limits, costs, and failure responses.
- [x] Every fixture has provenance and an expected classification, including unknown cases.
- [x] A documented disconnect experiment identifies the available recovery path and its coverage limits.
- [x] No credential, private watchlist, or unsolicited personal identity information is committed.
- [x] A go/no-go decision permits the wallet-first path or lists the exact blocked capability.

## Completion evidence

Completed in merged [PR #30](https://github.com/nhattruong0204/wallet-observer/pull/30), commit `4e15c225fa98e40260a0ebe9773c7e46fd25c454`.

- [Source contract](https://github.com/nhattruong0204/wallet-observer/blob/main/docs/data-source-contract.md), [decision](https://github.com/nhattruong0204/wallet-observer/blob/main/docs/decisions/0001-solana-source.md), and [acceptance evidence](https://github.com/nhattruong0204/wallet-observer/blob/main/docs/acceptance/WO-002.md).
- Seven sanitized real captures cover the eight requested cases plus nonempty outage recovery.
- A five-minute disconnect missed one transaction; bounded history recovered it and matched the RPC reference.
- `make lint test fixtures` passed: 26 offline tests and seven fixture checks. No CI checks are configured yet.
- 27 HTTP requests and one consumed event imply 154 estimated credits; actual provider billing delta is unavailable.
- Publication scan found no actual API key or supplied wallet address.

GO for the bounded wallet-first path. Complete owner coverage, arbitrary outage recovery, reorg/finalization handling, unknown-route economics and FOMO fields remain explicitly unqualified or disabled. Production collector and normalizer implementation remain subsequent issues.

issues.title: [WO-004] Implement PostgreSQL migrations, canonical identities, and durable jobs
issues.body:
<!-- wallet-observer-task:WO-004 -->

**Milestone:** First live

**Plan:** [BUILD_PLAN.md](https://github.com/nhattruong0204/wallet-observer/blob/main/BUILD_PLAN.md)

**Website first (2026-10-05):** Deliver the desktop-browser website and its supporting services. Native mobile apps, installable PWA features, device push, mobile-specific UX and mobile acceptance gates are deferred. Existing responsive behavior may remain. See the [scope decision](https://github.com/nhattruong0204/wallet-observer/blob/main/docs/decisions/0003-website-first.md).

## Why we need this

Stable identities and transactional persistence prevent duplicated trades, mismatched tokens, and lost work when the collector or API restarts.

## What to do

- Create the initial relational schema and migrations for watches, identities, source records, events, executions, quotes, checkpoints, jobs, and notifications.
- Define uniqueness constraints, precision, event revisions, and a committed delivery sequence.

## How to implement

1. Use chain plus canonical address for wallets/tokens; preserve Solana case. Separate human labels from evidence-bearing account-wallet links.
2. Deduplicate raw source IDs and economic executions with chain/signature/instruction identity where available. Store raw payloads with bounded retention.
3. Use integer/high-precision numeric quantities and decimal values; store UTC timestamps and explicit unknown/missing states.
4. Write canonical mutations and an outbox row in the same transaction. A single ordered dispatcher must assign/persist a committed delivery sequence; do not use a pre-commit sequence as the replay watermark.
5. Implement migrations and indexed access paths. Keep jobs claimable with a lease and bounded retries; one process may still crash mid-job.

## Expected files and deliverables

- `backend/migrations/`
- `backend/src/wallet_observer/db/`
- `docs/data-model.md`
- `tests/integration/test_persistence.py`

## Dependencies

- [WO-002](https://github.com/nhattruong0204/wallet-observer/issues/2)
- [WO-003](https://github.com/nhattruong0204/wallet-observer/issues/3)

## Definition of done

- [x] Migrations apply to an empty database and an upgrade path is documented.
- [x] Duplicate fixture ingestion does not create extra executions.
- [x] Two distinct same-amount swaps remain distinct.
- [x] A rollback does not advance the safe source checkpoint or emit a phantom committed event.
- [x] Precision, address case, and chain separation survive a database round-trip.
- [x] No user, billing, entitlement, quota, or session tables are introduced.

## Completion evidence

Verified on 2026-10-05 in the pinned devcontainer. See the [acceptance record](https://github.com/nhattruong0204/wallet-observer/blob/main/docs/acceptance/WO-004.md), [data-model and migration contract](https://github.com/nhattruong0204/wallet-observer/blob/main/docs/data-model.md), and [development commands](https://github.com/nhattruong0204/wallet-observer/blob/main/docs/development.md).

- `make doctor`, repeated `make migrate`, `make lint`, and builds passed.
- With an explicit disposable `TEST_DATABASE_URL`, `make test` passed **85 Python tests (24 PostgreSQL integration checks) and 4 frontend tests**. All seven existing source fixture checks passed.
- Integration checks proved duplicate/same-amount identity behavior, exact precision and chain separation, rollback and disconnected-producer safety, committed delivery ordering, revision corrections, lease fencing and bounded retries/retention.
- Installed-wheel migrations applied and repeated successfully with SQL checksums matching source.
- A real PostgreSQL restart preserved the committed fixture, checkpoint, pending publication and leased job; recovery produced one delivery.

No provider probe or Telegram message was sent. Production collection/normalization, handler scheduling, live browser transport and alert sending remain later issues. Migrations are forward-only; backup recovery is documented. CI setup is #15; this evidence is from local checks. The implementation PR is linked from this issue.

Always-on ingestion is the source of the live feed. The browser must not be responsible for keeping collection running.

- Implement the qualified outbound stream adapter and persist raw source events.
- Manage watch-filter changes, reconnect/backoff, bounded processing, and source health.

## How to implement

1. Hide provider payloads behind a small adapter interface: capabilities, subscription updates, event envelope, history lookup, and health.
2. Prefer the qualified outbound WebSocket path so the private dashboard needs no public webhook endpoint. If an approved provider requires callbacks, expose only a separately authenticated ingestion route.
3. Persist accepted source records and durable processing work before advancing a safe source checkpoint.
4. Handle disconnects, subscription rejection, rate limiting, malformed payloads, and provider-schema changes. Quarantine unrecognized payloads instead of discarding them silently.
5. Bound queues and retries. On watch changes, avoid overlapping subscriptions causing unbounded duplicate delivery.

issues.title: [WO-007] Normalize swaps and reconcile transaction confirmation
issues.body:
<!-- wallet-observer-task:WO-007 -->

**Milestone:** First live

**Plan:** [BUILD_PLAN.md](https://github.com/nhattruong0204/wallet-observer/blob/main/BUILD_PLAN.md)

**Website first (2026-10-05):** Deliver the desktop-browser website and its supporting services. Native mobile apps, installable PWA features, device push, mobile-specific UX and mobile acceptance gates are deferred. Existing responsive behavior may remain. See the [scope decision](https://github.com/nhattruong0204/wallet-observer/blob/main/docs/decisions/0003-website-first.md).

## Why we need this

A decoded instruction or incoming transfer does not necessarily mean the watched wallet bought a token. Incorrect attribution would contaminate every downstream view and alert.

## What to do

- Convert supported source records into canonical economic executions and explicit unknown/unsupported events.
- Separate trade execution outcome from chain confirmation and preserve revisions.

## How to implement

1. Attribute balance changes and execution legs to the watched wallet; account for fees, wrapped SOL, token-account creation/rent, and routed swaps.
2. Merge legs only with sufficient transaction/instruction evidence. Keep two independent orders or swaps separate even if time and amount match.
3. Use fixture-driven route handlers for programs proved in WO-002. Unsupported routes remain visible with a reason and source link.
4. Track observed/confirmed/finalized/corrected chain facts without inventing off-chain FOMO order states. Failed transactions cannot contribute to confirmed trade totals.
5. Apply later status changes idempotently; publish revisions and reverse any now-invalid derived contributions.

## Expected files and deliverables

- `backend/src/wallet_observer/trades/`
- `tests/unit/test_trade_normalization.py`
- `tests/integration/test_reconciliation.py`

- [WO-004](https://github.com/nhattruong0204/wallet-observer/issues/4)
- [WO-006](https://github.com/nhattruong0204/wallet-observer/issues/6)

- [ ] Representative buy, sell, transfer, failed, routed, and wrapped-SOL fixtures classify correctly.
- [ ] Amounts retain raw precision and fees are distinguished from acquired/sold quantity.
- [ ] Transfer-only records do not trigger buy/sell alerts.
- [ ] Duplicate delivery creates one appropriate execution; distinct swaps are not collapsed.
- [ ] Confirmation/status corrections are reflected in history with provenance.

issues.title: [WO-008] Implement durable recovery, bounded backfill, and gap reporting
issues.body:
<!-- wallet-observer-task:WO-008 -->

**Milestone:** First live

**Plan:** [BUILD_PLAN.md](https://github.com/nhattruong0204/wallet-observer/blob/main/BUILD_PLAN.md)

**Website first (2026-10-05):** Deliver the desktop-browser website and its supporting services. Native mobile apps, installable PWA features, device push, mobile-specific UX and mobile acceptance gates are deferred. Existing responsive behavior may remain. See the [scope decision](https://github.com/nhattruong0204/wallet-observer/blob/main/docs/decisions/0003-website-first.md).

## Why we need this

A tracker that loses activity whenever the VPS or provider disconnects cannot support dependable histories or signals.

## What to do

- Recover missed source activity using persisted checkpoints and the qualified history endpoint.
- Separate live delivery from historical replay and expose unrecoverable coverage gaps.

## How to implement

1. Persist a per-source/per-watch recovery boundary supported by the provider. Use an overlap window and stable deduplication rather than assuming a perfect replay cursor.
2. Process backfill through the same normalization code as live events, tagged with replay provenance and alert eligibility.
3. Bound backfill depth, page count, concurrency, and credits. Persist job progress and retry leases so interruption is resumable.
4. Define the source-history limit and record a gap if it prevents complete recovery. Never advance a checkpoint over failed unpersisted work.
5. Maintain event occurrence order separately from the ordered delivery log; late source events are valid.

## Expected files and deliverables

- `backend/src/wallet_observer/recovery/`
- `tests/integration/test_recovery.py`
- `docs/recovery.md`

## Dependencies

- [WO-004](https://github.com/nhattruong0204/wallet-observer/issues/4)
- [WO-006](https://github.com/nhattruong0204/wallet-observer/issues/6)
- [WO-007](https://github.com/nhattruong0204/wallet-observer/issues/7)

## Definition of done

- [ ] An outage-and-restart exercise recovers known missing fixtures without duplicates.
- [ ] Live ingestion can continue while a bounded backfill runs.
- [ ] Historical imports do not flood Telegram.
- [ ] A second interruption resumes rather than restarting an unlimited scan.
- [ ] Coverage gaps are returned by the API and visible to the user.
- [ ] A database transaction rollback does not falsely move the recovery boundary.

## Completion evidence

## What to do

- Resolve token metadata and cache current quotes for tokens in the watch scope.
- Keep execution valuation separate from current market valuation.

1. Use chain/address keys and timestamped provider adapters. Request only observed or opened tokens, with bounded TTL refresh and concurrency.
2. Retain raw execution quantities; compute historical USD values only from a sufficiently contemporaneous and attributable price source.
3. Expose price source, observation time, stale/missing state, and available market fields. Do not treat missing market cap or liquidity as zero.
4. Reject late stale updates overwriting newer quotes. Handle duplicate symbols, multiple pools, decimal corrections, and token-not-found responses.
5. Batch requests where the provider supports it and surface usage against the configured monthly budget.

## How to implement

1. Read the RayBot assessment and current Helius source contract. The owner reports Pro 200; the custom-webhook documentation lists 3 slots for that tier. Verify the actual entitlement, API access, webhook limit/used slots and applicable notification caps using owner-provided configuration. Do not infer the tier from payment amount or confuse Discord webhook limits with custom HTTPS callbacks.
2. Use server-side API credentials from ignored local configuration. Start with read-only list calls. A later live capture must be explicitly opted in: propose at most 3 existing watched Solana wallets, 10 minutes, 100 accepted events and 30 control-plane requests, paced below the documented API limit. 3. Use an isolated temporary HTTPS receiver for the bounded experiment; document and clean up only its own destination. Preserve raw captures privately and sanitize approved fixtures with provenance. Documentation examples are vendor examples, not our live captures; placeholder signatures cannot serve as independently verified transactions.
4. Resolve signature-versus-UUID delivery headers, ID stability across retries/destinations, verification timeout differences, retry schedule/retention and event ordering. Determine slot/commitment, timestamp meaning, execution/instruction identity, actor attribution and parser failures. Do not synthesize missing fields.
5. Compare actual raw token quantities/decimals, SOL versus WSOL representation, fee-inclusive owner deltas versus trade legs, price timestamps and position units against qualified chain responses. Record rounding/conflicts, missing opening history and corrections. Confirm signal schemas and identities separately.
6. Record the destination and global/per-wallet filter configuration, burst grouping, signal-only settings, auto-pause and expiry behavior. Deliberate silence is not complete coverage. Test repeat delivery and a bounded interruption only on the isolated destination; report unrecoverable RayBot gaps honestly.
7. Verify whether a supported history/export path exists and what personal storage/use is allowed. No public history/replay API was found in this docs review. Preserve unanswered questions as capability blockers, not an assumed negative provider answer.

issues.body:
<!-- wallet-observer-task:WO-031 -->

**Milestone:** Optional RayBot

**Status:** Planned; enable only after the required RayBot capability passes qualification. Optional to first-live delivery.

**Assessment:** [RayBot feasibility review](https://github.com/nhattruong0204/wallet-observer/blob/main/docs/raybot-integration-assessment.md).

## Why we need this

RayBot callbacks must survive restarts and retries without exposing the private dashboard or trusting unverified event facts.

## What to do

- Add one optional authenticated HTTPS ingestion route on the existing API and durable processing in the existing worker/PostgreSQL.
- Expose RayBot destination health and an operator runbook; deployment activation uses #17’s private-access boundary.

## How to implement

1. Keep RayBot disabled by default. Require an independent high-entropy callback secret, HTTPS and constant-time authorization validation. User-Agent is diagnostic only. Do not invent HMAC signatures, trusted IP ranges or provider certificates absent a verified contract.
2. Accept the verified test event separately without creating a trade. For accepted activity, atomically persist the source envelope, payload representation and job before returning 2xx. Bound body size, parse depth and work; target an acknowledgement below one second and process heavy work asynchronously.
3. Keep delivery attempt ID, destination, chain transaction ID and payload hash distinct. A signature may carry multiple wallet/event representations, while a retry may have a different transport ID. Preserve distinct evidence and make duplicate processing harmless according to the qualified contract.
4. Return retryable failure for temporary persistence failures. Persist bounded quarantine for authenticated unknown schemas where possible, then alert on incompatibility. Define permanent rejection deliberately because documented 4xx responses are not retried; include overload and disk-full behavior.
5. Reuse existing source-health/retention mechanisms from #16. Record receipts, duplicate counts, queue age, rejected/quarantined events, destination send/pause/expired status and failure count. Silence alone cannot prove a fault or completeness; reconcile health with a paced control-plane status read.
6. Provide reviewed provisioning/rotation/pause/removal instructions for a dedicated destination. Pause/resume affects attached wallet state; do not automatically resume after repeated failure. Register only the selected watch subset, respect shared API budgets, and isolate the public callback route from all private app/admin endpoints.

<!-- wallet-observer-task:WO-032 -->

**Milestone:** Optional RayBot

**Status:** Planned; enable only after the required RayBot capability passes qualification. Optional to first-live delivery.

## Why we need this

The same trade observed by Helius and RayBot must contribute once to the website and alerts, while disagreements remain inspectable.

## What to do

- Attach RayBot evidence to verified canonical executions through the existing revision and outbox model.
- Keep unmatched or conflicting observations visible as source evidence without creating unsupported trades.

## How to implement

1. Match by chain/transaction, watched actor, qualified instruction identity and verified owner/token flows. RayBot’s documented transaction-level envelope lacks instruction indices; fetch qualified chain detail when needed. Never assign index 0 or match only amounts/time/fee payer to satisfy the schema.
2. Separate delivery identity from execution identity and classify each wallet independently. Handle multiple swaps in a signature, incidental watched accounts, multiple destinations, changed payloads and retried deliveries.
3. Use exact raw integer strings plus verified decimals and chain/address identity. Parse numeric enrichment lexemes as Decimal; preserving their text does not repair upstream rounding. Quarantine contradictory raw quantities and do not rebuild raw values from rounded display amounts.
4. Keep RayBot balance deltas, economic trade legs, rent/fees and native SOL/WSOL separate. Failed transactions, ordinary transfers, liquidity and fee claims cannot become successful buys. Missing parser detail remains unknown.
5. Verify success, slot and confirmation via the qualified chain path; failed:false is not finalization. Preserve both source observations on disagreement and append canonical corrections transactionally. RayBot delivery must not advance a Helius safe checkpoint.
6. Use #8’s bounded chain backfill for canonical coverage. Track RayBot filter/receipt gaps separately: recovery of chain transactions does not reconstruct RayBot-only prices, positions or signals. Keep ambiguous events out of position totals, consensus and notifications.
7. Corroboration should add provenance without sending a second trade alert. #14 must key delivery intent to canonical identity and apply correction policy, not provider arrival count.
